label: abstract-algebra
tail:
Done. Both track files are complete; every published id I cited is verified against disk.

## What I found on arrival

The previous instance of this lane had already written the reconciliation (§II.1) and the **entire Galois block, GA-1…GA-4** — the headline gap — before the session limit cut it off. I continued rather than restarted.

## What I added

**`plan-algebra-track.md`** (2890 → 4644 lines): AA-14 symmetric polynomials, AA-15 algebraic extensions/degree/finite fields, LA-9 diagonalisation, LA-10 triangularisation and Jordan form, LA-12 inner product spaces, X-1 the fundamental theorem of algebra, X-2 the spectral theorem and SVD — plus the well-definedness table, choice-strength ledger, coverage harvest and amendments.

**`plan-algebra-track-expansion.md`** (1856 → 2822 lines): AG-3, AG-4, MOD-3, MOD-4, MOD-5, the RT block, amendments and the orchestrator report.

## The findings that changed the most

- **AG-4 lost nine planned items to disk.** The whole *p*-group toolkit is published at `group-actions-and-cayleys-theorem`, and the entire nilpotency series theory landed on AG-2, not AG-4 as Part I planned. Similarly three of AG-3's automorphism items are already published.
- **The library uses "the dihedral group" in five published examples and defines it nowhere.** All five are B-page leaves, so AG-3 must build it natively.
- **Noetherian should be defined by "every submodule is finitely generated", not by ACC.** Every source proves the equivalence by extracting an infinite strictly increasing chain — dependent choice — and none flags it. Since this track mints the definition for `commutative-algebra`, I put it on the choice-free side.
- **The spectral theorem splits into steps at three different costs**, and only one needs the fundamental theorem of algebra. That let me move most of it down to LA-12 (order 94) as a *conditional* theorem, with X-2 discharging the hypothesis — mostly legal 47 places earlier in reading order.
- **The RT block runs over a splitting field with a bilinear character pairing**, not over ℂ with a Hermitian one. This removes RT-3's dependence on the inner-product page entirely. It also caught a trap: "k ⊇ μₑ implies k is a splitting field" is Brauer's theorem, which Webb states *without proof*.
- **Algebraic closure needs BPIT, not Zorn**, and is not a ZF theorem (Banaschewski 1992). The textbook Zorn proofs use it for convenience.

Two things I corrected in Part II text written earlier in this same run: GA-1 now takes the one-step Gilmer/Milne route to the algebraic closure instead of the ω-iteration (removes ~5 items), and cites the Frobenius from AA-15 rather than minting a second one.

## Sources

Four research subagents obtained ~25 sources in full text — Milne, Clark, Ash, Axler, Hoffman & Kunze, Treil, Macdonald, Knapp, Wisbauer, Crawley-Boevey, Webb, Etingof, Artin, ~40 Conrad blurbs. Full heading enumerations are in `research/subjects-01-dispatch/aa-harvest-*.md`; §II.12 indexes them with a two-treatments check per pair.

**Not everything is met.** §II.12.b records ten gaps honestly rather than papering over them — Cauchy interlacing and Weyl are single-sourced and there only as exercises; the right-Noetherian-not-left-Noetherian witness is unsourced and must be verified or dropped; five results the scaffold uses are proved in nothing I obtained and must be proved inline. Isaacs and Fulton–Harris were unobtainable.

**Blockers: none.** I wrote only the two files I own — nothing under `items/`, `library/`, or `plan-spec.json`, and no gates run. The other modified track files in `git status` belong to the concurrent combinatorics and category-theory lanes. Nothing is committed; that is the orchestrator's call.
